title: MBBS in India: Education to Practice
subtitle: Understanding the pathway, challenges, and opportunities in Indian medical education.

slides.title: MBBS in India: From Classroom to Clinic
What is MBBS in India?
slides.subtitle: Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery
bullets: 5.5-year undergraduate medical degree plus 1-year internship.
Governed by Medical Council of India (MCI) and NMC regulations.
Entry via NEET-UG: 18-lakh+ candidates compete annually.
Produces 100,000+ doctors annually across 560+ institutions.

slides.title: Timeline: MBBS Journey in India
slides.subtitle: Key milestones from admission to licensing
bullets: Year 1-2: Pre-clinical sciences—anatomy, physiology, biochemistry.
Year 3-4: Paraclinical and clinical training in major specialties.
Year 5: Internship with rotations across departments and hospitals.
Post-MBBS: FMGE exam required for international practice; NEET-PG for specialization.

slides.title: Admission Requirements & NEET-UG
bullets: 12th standard pass with Physics, Chemistry, Biology (PCB).
Minimum 50% aggregate; SC/ST/OBC: 40% marks required.
NEET-UG 2024: 720 marks out of 720; cutoff ~164-171.
Merit-based: 85% government seats; 15% deemed/private institution seats.

slides.title: Top Medical Colleges in India
slides.subtitle: NIRF Rankings 2024
bullets: AIIMS Delhi: gold standard; research-led, 5% acceptance rate.
CMC Vellore: oldest private medical college; strong clinical training.
Maulana Azad Medical College: central university; Delhi-based; highly competitive.

slides.title: Key Challenges in Indian MBBS
bullets: Infrastructure gap: overcrowded classrooms; limited lab equipment in tier-2/3 colleges.
High student-patient ratio hampering hands-on clinical experience for many.
2024: NMC revised curriculum to reduce outdated content; still evolving.
Exam-centric learning: rote memorization over critical thinking skills.

slides.title: Trend 1: Digital Health & Telemedicine Training
slides.subtitle: Integration into MBBS curriculum
bullets: 2023-2024: Major AIIMS and government colleges added telemedicine modules.
Example: AIIMS Delhi now conducts virtual OPD consultations with students observing.
NMC guidelines mandate digital literacy and e-health literacy for graduates.
Indian telehealth market growing at 45% CAGR; demand for trained doctors.

slides.title: Trend 2: Emphasis on Affordable Healthcare Access
bullets: 2024: MBBS syllabus now focuses on rural health and primary care.
Ayushman Bharat scheme requires 50% students to work in underserved areas.
Public health module strengthened in all government medical colleges.
Key insight: producing doctors for India's 900M+ population gaps.

slides.title: Post-MBBS Pathways & Licensing
bullets: NEET-PG: Gateway to 3-year specialization programs across all fields.
FMGE (Screening Test): mandatory for overseas practice; ~30% pass rate.
Clinical Practice Registration: state medical council registers doctors after internship.
2024: NEET-PG seats expanded to 47,000+ across recognized institutes.

slides.title: Career Outcomes & Employment Trends
bullets: 2023 data: 60% pursue specialization; 25% enter government service.
Private practice and corporate hospitals absorb 40% of graduates.
Brain drain: 8-10% migrate annually to USA, UK, Australia, Canada.
Emerging: startups in health tech hiring doctors for product and research roles.

slides.title: Future of MBBS: 2025-2030 Outlook
bullets: NMC planning AI-integrated diagnostics and clinical decision support training.
Competency-based education replacing traditional exams in progressive colleges.
Expected: 40% increase in medical seats by 2030 nationwide.
Note: Quality assurance remains key challenge as enrollment expands.

slides.title: Ready to Pursue MBBS?
bullets: Start NEET preparation early; focus on conceptual clarity over memorization.
